# Compliance determination — Inspection Authorization (IA): qualifications and authority with respect to major alterations

**Prepared in the Compliance Engineer role.** This is a regulatory interpretation of 14 CFR (eCFR current text) and FAA guidance. It is not legal advice for a specific applicant, and it is not a determination in a certificate-action or enforcement matter.

---

## 0. How the ask was read (state this back before relying on the answer)

| Term in the ask | Read as | If that reading is wrong |
|---|---|---|
| "inspection auth" | Inspection Authorization (IA), **14 CFR part 65, subpart D (§§ 65.91–65.95)** | A different authorization (e.g., part 145 repair-station approval, DAR/DER delegation) would have a completely different answer |
| "qualifications … regarding major alterations" | Answered **both** ways, kept separate: **(A) eligibility** — what an applicant must show to be issued an IA (§ 65.91), and **(B) authority/limits** — what the IA may do with a major alteration once issued (§ 65.95 with part 43) | Answering only (B) is the most common failure mode; the literal word "qualifications" is (A) |
| "FAA-AMT" | FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician program context — AMT Handbook (FAA-H-8083-30/-31 series), IA Information Guide, IA Airman Certification Standards | These are **guidance/testing standards, not regulation**. They corroborate; they never override the CFR |
| Source | eCFR current text (14 CFR), fetched this session; FAA guidance where noted | Text is date-sensitive — see § 9 |

**Scope exclusions:** part 121/135 operator-specific programs (except where § 65.95 itself carves out part 121), part 145 repair-station approval mechanics, military/foreign authority, and any specific applicant's factual eligibility.

---

## 1. Bottom line (one-page answer)

1. **There is no separate "major alteration qualification."** A person qualifies to act on major alterations by holding an **IA issued under 14 CFR 65.91**, and the major-alteration content is embedded in one specific eligibility element: **§ 65.91(c)(5)** — passing a written test on the ability to inspect for return to service **after major repairs and major alterations** (and annual/progressive inspections) under part 43. **[C]**
2. **The four other eligibility elements (§ 65.91(c)(1)–(4))** are general IA qualifications, not alteration-specific: 3-year A&P, 2 years actively engaged, fixed base of operations, equipment/facilities/inspection data. **[C]**
3. **Once issued, the IA's major-alteration authority is § 65.95(a)(1)** — inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part/appliance after a major repair or major alteration, **only if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**, and **excluding aircraft maintained under a part 121 continuous airworthiness program**. **[V]**
4. **The IA does not approve the alteration data.** The IA inspects **for conformity to approved data** and determines airworthiness/compatibility with prior repairs and alterations; the IA must **personally perform the inspection**. **[G]**
5. **A mechanic without an IA may perform a major alteration but may not approve it for return to service** — that approval comes from an IA, a part 145 repair station, a manufacturer under § 43.7(d)-type authority, or the FAA. **[C]**

---

## 2. Governing provisions map

| Provision | What it controls | Bearing on major alterations | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|
| **§ 65.91(a)–(c)** | Application; entitlement; **eligibility** | (c)(5) is the alteration/repair-specific qualification | [C] |
| **§ 65.92** | Duration — expires **March 31 of each odd-numbered year** | An expired IA has **zero** alteration-approval authority | [C] |
| **§ 65.93** | Renewal (activity options include major repairs/alterations) | Currency, not initial qualification | [C] — see § 8 |
| **§ 65.95(a)(1)** | **Privilege**: inspect and approve for return to service after major repair/alteration | The operative authority | **[V]** verbatim captured |
| **§ 65.95(a)(2)** | Annual / progressive inspections | Adjacent privilege, not alteration approval | **[V]** |
| **§ 43.3** | Who may *perform* maintenance/alterations | Performing ≠ approving | [C] |
| **§ 43.5** | Approval for return to service — preconditions (record entry, FAA form, flight-manual/limitations revision) | Conditions the IA's signature | [C] |
| **§ 43.7** | Who may *approve* for return to service | Places the IA in the approval chain | [C] |
| **§ 43.9** | Content/form/disposition of maintenance records | What the IA's approval must be supported by | [C] |
| **Part 43, App. A** | What counts as a **major alteration** (airframe, powerplant, propeller, appliance) | Classification gate — if it isn't major, no IA approval is required | [C] |
| **Part 43, App. B** | Recording of major repairs/alterations (FAA Form 337) | The IA signs the approval-for-return-to-service block | [C] |
| **Part 1 (definitions)** | "Major alteration" / "major repair" definitions | Feeds App. A classification | [C] |
| **§ 91.409 / § 91.417** | Annual inspection; record retention | Where the IA's part 43 actions land in operating rules | [C] |

**Flag legend:** **[V]** = verbatim regulatory/guidance text captured this session from the cited URL. **[C]** = section cited from 14 CFR; wording below is a faithful paraphrase and should be confirmed against the eCFR page for that section before being quoted in a filing. **[G]** = FAA guidance/testing material, non-regulatory.

---

## 3. (A) Eligibility — the qualifications themselves, § 65.91(c)

An applicant who meets § 65.91(c) is **entitled** to an IA (§ 65.91(b)); application is made on the form and in the manner the Administrator prescribes (§ 65.91(a)). **[C]**

| # | Qualification | Threshold | Why it matters to major alterations |
|---|---|---|---|
| (c)(1) | Holds a **currently effective mechanic certificate with both Airframe and Powerplant ratings**, each currently effective and in effect a total of at least **3 years** | 3 years | The IA is an overlay on an A&P; no A&P, no IA, no alteration approval |
| (c)(2) | **Actively engaged** for at least the **2-year period** before application in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR | 2 years | Recent hands-on currency before being trusted to judge conformity |
| (c)(3) | **Fixed base of operations** where reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week (need not be where the IA exercises the authorization) | — | Traceability/availability of the approving person |
| (c)(4) | Has available the **equipment, facilities, and inspection data** necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or related parts/appliances | — | Directly enables "conformity to approved data" — the core alteration test |
| **(c)(5)** | **Passes a written test** on ability to inspect according to safety standards for **returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations**, and for annual and progressive inspections under part 43 | — | **This is the alteration-specific qualification.** The test content is where major-alteration inspection competency is actually certified |

**Engineering note on (c)(5):** the regulation does not itemize test subjects; the subject matter is set through the FAA's IA knowledge-test/Airman Certification Standards process. Use the ACS as the *test blueprint*, not as an additional regulatory requirement. **[G]**

---

## 4. (B) Authority and limits once qualified — § 65.95

**Verbatim, § 65.95(a) [V]:**

> "(a) The holder of an inspection authorization may—
> (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and
> (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter."

**Verbatim, FAA IA Information Guide [G]:**

> "The basic functions of the holder of an inspection authorization (IA) are set forth in Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR) part 65, § 65.95."

> "A primary responsibility of the holder of an IA is to determine airworthiness by inspecting repairs or alterations for conformity to approved data, and assuring that the aircraft is in a condition for safe operation.
> During inspection of major repairs or major alterations, the holder of an IA must also determine that they are compatible with previous repairs and alterations that have been made to the aircraft.
> The holder of an IA must personally perform the inspection."

### 4.1 Four conditions embedded in § 65.95(a)(1) — treat as gating checks

| # | Condition | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The item is an **aircraft or related part or appliance** | Out-of-scope article → no IA approval under this paragraph |
| 2 | The work is a **major repair or major alteration** per part 43 / part 1 | If minor, an IA approval is not the required mechanism (see § 43.7/§ 43.9 chain) |
| 3 | The work was done **in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator** | **No approved data = no IA approval authority.** The IA cannot cure a data deficiency by signing |
| 4 | The aircraft is **not** maintained under a **part 121 continuous airworthiness program** | Carve-out is in the regulatory text itself; approval must come through the operator's program |

### 4.2 What the IA may **not** do (frequent misreadings)

- **May not approve technical data.** Approving data (STC, field approval, DER) is a different function. The IA approves *return to service after conformity to already-approved data*. **[V]/[G]**
- **May not delegate the inspection.** "The holder of an IA must personally perform the inspection." **[G]**
- **May not ignore prior work.** Must determine compatibility with previous repairs and alterations. **[G]**
- **May not exercise any privilege with an expired or unrenewed authorization** (§ 65.92). **[C]**
- **Is not a repair station.** Part 145 approval authority is separate and is not conferred by an IA. **[C]**

---

## 5. The part 43 chain — perform vs. approve

| Step | Who | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Perform the major alteration | Any person authorized under § 43.3 (e.g., certificated mechanic) | § 43.3 **[C]** |
| Determine it *is* major | Classification against part 1 definitions and **part 43 appendix A** (airframe / powerplant / propeller / appliance lists) | Part 1; App. A **[C]** |
| Approve for return to service | **IA** under § 65.95(a)(1); or part 145 repair station; or manufacturer; or the Administrator, per § 43.7 | §§ 43.7, 65.95 **[C]/[V]** |
| Preconditions to that approval | Maintenance record entry made (§ 43.9); FAA form (Form 337 for major repair/alteration, App. B) executed as prescribed; operating limitations/flight data revised if changed (§ 43.5) | §§ 43.5, 43.9; App. B **[C]** |
| Record | FAA Form 337 — Major Repair and Alteration; IA signs the **approval-for-return-to-service** block | App. B **[C]** |

**Key compliance point:** a major alteration performed by an A&P who holds no IA is a lawful performance but an **unapproved** return to service until an authorized approver signs. That is the single most common real-world defect this question is usually aimed at.

---

## 6. Practical qualification-verification procedure (apply to a specific IA before relying on a signature)

Run in order; stop at first failure.

1. **Certificate check** — currently effective mechanic certificate, Airframe **and** Powerplant, in effect ≥ 3 years. (§ 65.91(c)(1)) **[C]**
2. **IA issuance check** — IA actually issued (it is an *authorization*, not a rating on the mechanic certificate). (§ 65.91) **[C]**
3. **Currency check** — expiration date is **March 31 of an odd-numbered year** and has not passed; renewal evidence on file. (§§ 65.92, 65.93) **[C]**
4. **Article check** — is the item an aircraft/part/appliance, and is it excluded by the part 121 continuous-airworthiness carve-out? (§ 65.95(a)(1)) **[V]**
5. **Classification check** — major alteration per part 1 + part 43 App. A? If minor, route through § 43.7/§ 43.9 instead. **[C]**
6. **Data check** — is there Administrator-approved technical data covering the alteration? No → the IA has no approval authority; escalate (STC/field approval/DER). **[V]**
7. **Personal-inspection check** — did the signing IA personally perform the inspection, and does the record show compatibility with prior repairs/alterations? **[G]**
8. **Paperwork check** — § 43.9 record entry made; Form 337 executed with the approval-for-return-to-service block signed; flight manual/limitations revised if affected (§ 43.5). **[C]**

---

## 7. "FAA-AMT" — how the AMT material fits (and does not fit)

| Source | Status | Proper use |
|---|---|---|
| 14 CFR part 65 subpart D; part 43; part 1 | **Binding regulation** | The answer |
| FAA IA Information Guide | Guidance | Corroborates the § 65.95 function and the personal-inspection/compatibility duties **[G]** |
| AMT Handbook (FAA-H-8083-30/-31 series) | Guidance/handbook | Training/context only; never cite as the requirement |
| IA Airman Certification Standards | Test blueprint | Explains what § 65.91(c)(5) is tested against **[G]** |
| FAA Order 8300.x series | Internal FAA guidance | Not applicant-facing requirements |

**Citation discipline:** cite the CFR section for every requirement; cite guidance only as corroboration and label it as guidance. Do not cite a handbook page as if it were regulatory text.

---

## 8. Appendix — currency and renewal (§§ 65.92, 65.93) — supplementary, flagged [C]

Included only because renewal activity options reference major repairs/alterations; **verify against the eCFR § 65.93 page before quoting.**

- **§ 65.92:** each inspection authorization **expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year**.
- **§ 65.93(a):** renewal requires the holder still meet § 65.91(c)(1)–(4) and, **within the 12-month period before application**, have done at least one of:
  1. performed at least one **annual inspection for each 90 days** elapsed since issuance/renewal;
  2. performed at least **two major repairs or major alterations**;
  3. performed or supervised and approved at least **one progressive inspection**;
  4. attended and completed a refresher course of **not less than 8 hours** of instruction acceptable to the Administrator; or
  5. passed an **oral test** by an FAA inspector.

These five are **alternatives**, not cumulative. None of these figures modifies the § 65.91(c) eligibility thresholds in § 3 — they are separate, independent thresholds from a different section.

---

## 9. Verification status, date sensitivity, and what to confirm before use

- **Access date for fetched material:** 2026-11-15 (per this session's retrieval timestamps).
- **Verbatim-verified this session [V]:** § 65.95(a)(1)–(2); the two IA Information Guide passages quoted in § 4.
- **Cited but not quoted verbatim this session [C]:** §§ 65.91, 65.92, 65.93, 43.3, 43.5, 43.7, 43.9, part 43 appendices A and B, part 1 definitions, §§ 91.409, 91.417.
- **Before any use in a filing, training record, or enforcement response:** open each [C] section on eCFR and confirm wording; eCFR text is current-as-of-access and can change by rulemaking.
- **Known soft spot:** § 65.93 renewal wording (activity options, 90-day and 8-hour figures) is the least-verified part of this deliverable; it is supplementary to the ask and is separated here so it cannot contaminate the core answer.

---

## 10. Answer as it should be recorded

**14 CFR 65.91(c)** — with the alteration-specific element at **§ 65.91(c)(5)** (written test on inspecting for return to service after major repairs and major alterations) — and, for the authority that qualification enables, **§ 65.95(a)(1)**, read with **14 CFR part 43** (§§ 43.5, 43.7, 43.9; appendices A and B). verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) and Major Alterations — Regulatory Answer (14 CFR / FAA-AMT)

**Primary citation (the answer): 14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1)** — "Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations." The parent section is § 65.95; the eligibility ("qualification") chain that must be satisfied before § 65.95(a)(1) authority exists is § 65.91, § 65.92, and § 65.93. The surrounding paperwork/return-to-service obligations live in 14 CFR Part 43, principally §§ 43.5, 43.7, 43.9, 43.13 and Appendix B (FAA Form 337).

Source basis: eCFR, Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter D, Part 65, Subpart D — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D (fetched 2026-11-15T04:31:41Z, sha256 1dc594967131); FAA *Inspection Authorization Information Guide* — https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/ia_info_guide.pdf (fetched 2026-11-15T04:31:42Z, sha256 ece24efe31ea).

---

## 0. Scope decision (stated, not assumed silently)

The phrase "qualifications for inspection auth regarding major alterations" reads two ways. Both are answered below, but the value returned is the **authority** provision, because that is how the FAA itself frames the topic:

> "This publication provides guidance for persons who conduct annual and progressive inspections and approve major repairs and/or major alterations of aircraft holding or eligible to hold a[n inspection authorization]" — FAA IA Information Guide (fetched 2026-11-15T04:31:42Z).

- Reading A (returned as the value): what an IA holder is qualified/authorized to do when a major alteration is presented for approval — **§ 65.95(a)(1)**.
- Reading B (answered in §2 below): what a person must hold/experience to obtain the IA at all — **§ 65.91** (with § 65.92, § 65.93).

Jurisdiction assumed: U.S.-registered aircraft under 14 CFR exclusively. Output is a regulatory summary with citations, not a legal opinion on any individual's eligibility.

---

## 1. The operative rule, verbatim

**14 CFR § 65.95(a):**

> "The holder of an inspection authorization may—
> (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and
> (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.11, 43.13, and 91.409 of this chapter."
> — eCFR Part 65 Subpart D, fetched 2026-11-15T04:31:41Z, sha256 1dc594967131.

### 1.1 Parsed into the four conditions an IA must actually satisfy

| # | Condition | Regulatory hook | What it means operationally |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **Holder** of a currently effective inspection authorization | § 65.95(a) opening; §§ 65.91, 65.92, 65.93 | The authority is personal to the certificate holder and is not delegable. An A&P without an IA cannot exercise it. |
| C2 | **Subject** is an aircraft or related part/appliance, **excluding** aircraft maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program | § 65.95(a)(1) parenthetical | Part 121 CAMP aircraft are outside IA approval authority; those go through the operator's approved program/repair station. |
| C3 | The major repair/alteration was **accomplished in accordance with Part 43** | § 65.95(a)(1); Part 43 (incl. § 43.13) | Workmanship/methods/data-use rules of Part 43 must be met; the IA is approving a Part 43-compliant alteration. |
| C4 | The work was done **in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator** | § 65.95(a)(1), final clause | **This is the gating qualification.** No FAA-approved technical data = nothing an IA can approve against. The IA's signature is a conformity/return-to-service act, **not** a data-approval act. |

**The single most important practical point:** an IA cannot *create* approved data. If the alteration has no approved data (TC/STC/approved drawing or other Administrator-approved data), the data itself must be approved by the FAA (field approval route, FAA Form 337 with FAA approval) *before* the IA can approve for return to service. Conflating these two acts is the most common error in this subject area.

---

## 2. Prerequisite qualifications to hold the IA (Reading B)

These are the qualifications that must exist **before** § 65.95(a)(1) authority can be exercised at all. *Verification status: paraphrased from the structure of Part 65 Subpart D; the specific wording and figures below are flagged for confirmation against current eCFR text before being quoted as verbatim regulation.*

| Requirement | Citation | Detail (verify verbatim at eCFR) |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanic certificate with **both** Airframe and Powerplant ratings, currently effective and in effect for a total of at least **3 years** | § 65.91(a)(1) | IA requires A&P; a single-rating mechanic is ineligible. |
| Actively engaged in maintaining aircraft under Part 65 for at least **2 years** | § 65.91(a)(2) | Recent, practical maintenance activity. |
| **Fixed base of operations** at which the applicant can be located for a reasonable time | § 65.91(a)(3) | Prevents a purely roving credential. |
| Available **equipment, facilities, and inspection data** necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or related parts/appliances | § 65.91(a)(4) | This is the facilities/tools prong; it is the one most often failed on surveillance. |
| Meets the renewal/currency requirements of **§ 65.93** | § 65.91(a)(5) | See row below. |
| **Duration / expiration** on a biennial cycle, expiring March 31 of odd-numbered years | § 65.92 | Confirm exact text; the practical effect is that an IA must be renewed every 2 years. |
| **Renewal** requirements (recent activity and/or refresher training) | § 65.93 | Confirm exact hours/activities at eCFR; **no hour figure is asserted here** because it was not verified from a fetched passage. |
| Underlying mechanic recent-experience rule | § 65.83 | Applies to exercise of the mechanic certificate itself (confirm the 24-month/6-month structure at eCFR). |

> **Correction to the project analysis:** the analysis attributes "1-year/2-year activity rules" to 14 CFR 65.71. That is wrong. **§ 65.71 is "Eligibility requirements: general" for the mechanic certificate** (age, English literacy, testing), and § 65.77 is the mechanic experience requirement. The **IA** eligibility and activity rules are **§ 65.91** and **§ 65.93**. Do not cite 65.71 for IA currency.

---

## 3. The Part 43 wrapper (what surrounds an IA's major-alteration approval)

| Step | Provision | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Is it major? | **14 CFR 1.1** (definitions of *major alteration* / *major repair*) and **Part 43 Appendix A** | Appendix A enumerates major alterations by category (airframe, powerplant, propeller, appliance). 1.1 supplies the general test (appreciably affects weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities; or not done per accepted practices / not elementary). |
| Who may perform | **§ 43.3** | Persons authorized to perform maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations. |
| Who may return to service | **§ 43.5**, **§ 43.7** | A certificated mechanic may approve for return to service work that person performed, **except** after a major repair or major alteration — that is where the IA (or a repair station/other § 43.7-authorized person) is required. |
| How performed | **§ 43.13** | Methods, techniques, practices, and use of data acceptable to the Administrator. |
| Record | **§ 43.9** | Description of work, date, signer's name and certificate number, and approval-for-return-to-service statement. |
| Paperwork for major alteration | **Part 43 Appendix B** | **FAA Form 337** is required for major repairs and major alterations; distribution is to the aircraft owner and to the FAA. *Confirm the exact submission timing in the current Appendix B text before relying on any hour figure — the commonly cited "48 hours" is not asserted here as verified.* |
| Guidance (non-binding) | AC 43.9-1F (Form 337 completion), AC 43-210-series (field approval data packages), FAA Order 8300.16 (major repair/alteration data approval) | Policy/instruction, **not** regulation. Do not cite these as the source of a legal requirement; cite Part 43/Part 65 for that and use these for method. |

---

## 4. Operating checklist — IA presented with a major alteration

1. **Confirm your own currency.** IA in effect (§ 65.92), renewal satisfied (§ 65.93), and you are the person who will sign.
2. **Classify.** Determine whether the change is a major alteration under 14 CFR 1.1 / Part 43 Appendix A. If minor, § 65.95(a)(1) is not the authority being used.
3. **Screen the aircraft.** If it is maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program, stop — § 65.95(a)(1) does not authorize your approval.
4. **Identify the approved technical data.** Locate the TC/STC/approved drawing/other Administrator-approved data that covers the alteration. If none exists, the alteration is **not** approvable by you; the data must first be approved by the FAA (field approval / Form 337 data block).
5. **Verify conformity.** Confirm the installation matches the approved data — parts, dimensions, materials, torques, clearances, weight and balance effect.
6. **Verify Part 43 compliance** of the work performed (§ 43.13), including any required tests/inspections (e.g., functional checks, ground run, flight test per the data).
7. **Record** per § 43.9 with a proper approval-for-return-to-service statement.
8. **Execute FAA Form 337** per Part 43 Appendix B; complete it per AC 43.9-1F.
9. **Distribute** per Appendix B — owner and FAA.
10. **File/retain** copies consistent with the operator's/owner's record requirements and any applicable § 91.417 obligations.

---

## 5. Limits — what an IA may **not** do on a major alteration

- May not approve an alteration that was **not** done in accordance with Administrator-approved technical data (§ 65.95(a)(1) condition C4).
- May not approve for aircraft maintained under a **Part 121 continuous airworthiness program** (§ 65.95(a)(1) parenthetical).
- May not use the IA to **create or approve data**; data approval is an FAA function.
- May not **delegate** the approval signature; the privilege attaches to the individual holder.
- Is acting outside Part 65 Subpart D if the IA is not currently effective.
- *Independence caution:* FAA guidance addresses an IA approving work the IA personally performed; no regulation is asserted here as an express bar. Treat this as a guidance/ethics question and confirm current FAA position before relying on either answer.

verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) — Qualifications Relevant to Major Alterations

**Governing code:** 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart E (Inspection Authorizations), §§ 65.91–65.95, read with 14 CFR Part 43 (particularly Appendix A, Appendix B, §§ 43.5, 43.7, 43.9). Source: eCFR (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-E), current text as retrieved 2026-11-15.

**Bottom line:** The IA is not a separate certificate — it is an authorization added to a mechanic certificate that already carries both Airframe and Powerplant ratings. There are three distinct things the question 'qualifications regarding major alterations' can mean, and all three apply: (1) the eligibility gate in § 65.91(c), whose written test is *expressly* about returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations; (2) the continuing conditions in §§ 65.92–65.93 that keep the authorization alive; and (3) the privilege/limitation in § 65.95(a)(1) that actually lets the holder approve a major alteration. An A&P mechanic without an IA cannot approve a major alteration for return to service.

---

## 1. Eligibility qualifications — § 65.91(c)

An applicant must satisfy **all five**. There is no partial qualification and no experience waiver.

| ¶ | Requirement | Substance |
|---|---|---|
| (c)(1) | **Certificate tenure — 3 years** | Holds a currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and **in effect for a total of at least 3 years**. An airframe-only or powerplant-only mechanic is ineligible. |
| (c)(2) | **Recent active engagement — 2 years** | Actively engaged, for at least the **2-year period before the application date**, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR Chapter I. This clock may run concurrently with the 3-year certificate tenure; it is not an additional 2 years stacked on top. |
| (c)(3) | **Fixed base of operations** | A fixed base at which the applicant can be reached in person or by telephone during a normal working week. It need **not** be where the authorization is exercised. |
| (c)(4) | **Equipment, facilities, and inspection data** | Must have available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or related parts/appliances. |
| (c)(5) | **Written test — the major-alteration hook** | Pass a written test on ability to inspect **according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations**, and for annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43. |

**This is the direct textual answer to the question.** Section 65.91(c)(5) is the only place in the eligibility rule that names major alterations, and it names them as a *tested competency*, not as an experience-hour requirement. The regulation sets no minimum number of major alterations the applicant must have previously performed or approved.

Procedural wrappers (recalled — verify against current text): § 65.91(a) application on the form and in the manner prescribed by the Administrator (FAA Form 8610-1); § 65.91(b) entitlement on meeting the section; § 65.91(d) a **30-day** wait before retesting after a failed § 65.91(c)(5) test.

---

## 2. Continuing conditions and renewal — §§ 65.92, 65.93

An IA is time-limited and condition-based; 'qualified' is not a one-time status.

- **Expiry / duration (§ 65.92).** Each inspection authorization expires **31 March of each odd-numbered year**. The holder may exercise the privileges **only while** holding a currently effective mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings currently effective. The authorization also ceases to be effective if the holder no longer has the fixed base of operations or the equipment/facilities/inspection data required by § 65.91(c)(3)–(4).
- **Renewal (§ 65.93).** Renewal is **for a 2-year period**; the applicant must present evidence **during March of each odd-numbered year** at the responsible Flight Standards office that they still meet § 65.91(c)(1)–(4), **and** must show qualifying activity.
- **Qualifying activity — § 65.93(a) list.** During the time the current authority was held, the applicant must show **one** of the following (the list is disjunctive — *not* cumulative):
  1. At least **one annual inspection for each 90 days** the current authority was held; or
  2. At least **two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days** the current authority was held *(confirmed verbatim: "Performed at least two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days that the applicant held the current authority; or")*; or
  3. Performed or supervised and approved at least **one progressive inspection** to standards prescribed by the Administrator; or
  4. Attended and successfully completed a refresher course acceptable to the Administrator of **not less than 8 hours** of instruction; or
  5. Passed an **oral test** by an FAA inspector to confirm current knowledge of applicable regulations and standards.
- **Structure of the requirement.** One qualifying activity must fall in the **first year** and one in the **second year** of the 2-year period. The rule does **not** require completing every alternative, and it does **not** prescribe a single aggregate number of events for the period — the § 65.93(a)(1)–(2) figures are **per-90-day rates**, not totals. Do not convert them into a count.
- **Short-tenure relief (§ 65.93(b), recalled — verify).** A holder whose authorization has been in effect for less than **90 days** before the expiration date need not comply with § 65.93(a)(1)–(5).

---

## 3. The privilege that actually covers major alterations — § 65.95

*(Confirmed verbatim from eCFR § 65.95, retrieved 2026-11-15.)*

> "The holder of an inspection authorization may—
> (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**; and
> (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter."

Four conditions are embedded in that single sentence, and all must be met:

1. **Person** — the approver must hold an IA. A mechanic certificate with A&P ratings alone authorizes approval after minor repairs/alterations and maintenance, not after a major alteration.
2. **Work** — it must be a *major* repair or *major* alteration within the Part 43 Appendix A definition.
3. **Data** — the work must have been done in accordance with **technical data approved by the Administrator**. The IA's signature does not cure unapproved data. If the alteration has no approved data, the route is a field approval (see AC 43-210A) — the IA cannot self-approve data.
4. **Aircraft** — the privilege is **excluded** for aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness program under **Part 121**. For those aircraft, the operator's/maintenance provider's own approved program governs.

Related Part 43 mechanics: § 43.5 (approval for return to service, including execution of the repair/alteration form); § 43.7 (persons authorized to approve for return to service — the narrow set that includes the IA); § 43.9 (maintenance record entries); **Appendix B** (recording major repairs and major alterations — FAA Form 337); § 65.95(b) (recalled) requires the IA, when exercising the authority, to sign the appropriate form and make the entries required by Part 43.

---

## 4. What counts as a 'major alteration' — Part 43, Appendix A

Appendix A is the operative definition, not Part 1.1. Paragraph (a) enumerates **major alterations** by category — airframe, powerplant, propeller, and appliance — using a consequence test: alterations that, if not done per the manufacturer's instructions or accepted practices, **may appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness**. Anything not listed as major is treated as **minor**. Appendix A(b) covers major repairs; Appendix A(c) covers preventive maintenance.

Practical consequence for the IA: the major/minor call determines *who may approve*, and the IA is the field-level person who may approve a major alteration — but only against approved data.

---

## 5. Decision procedure an AMT/IA applicant can apply directly

**A. Am I eligible to test?**
1. Is my mechanic certificate currently effective **with both** airframe and powerplant ratings? If no → ineligible.
2. Has it been in effect **at least 3 years** total? If no → wait.
3. Have I been actively engaged in maintaining Chapter I aircraft for the **2 years** before application? If no → wait.
4. Do I have a **fixed base** where I can be reached during a normal working week? If no → establish one.
5. Do I have the **equipment, facilities, and inspection data**? If no → acquire before applying.
6. Apply on the prescribed form, then pass the **written test** whose scope is defined by § 65.91(c)(5) — including return to service after major repairs and major alterations.

**B. May I approve this specific alteration for return to service?**
1. Is the aircraft maintained under a **Part 121** continuous airworthiness program? If yes → **stop**; § 65.95(a)(1) does not reach it.
2. Is the change a **major alteration** under Part 43 Appendix A? If minor → A&P authority applies; IA not required.
3. Was the work done in accordance with **technical data approved by the Administrator**? If no → obtain field approval/approved data first (AC 43-210A); do not sign.
4. Is my IA **currently effective** (A&P current, fixed base maintained, equipment/data available, not expired on 31 March of the odd year)? If no → stop.
5. Approve, sign **FAA Form 337** per Part 43 Appendix B, and make the § 43.9 record entries.

**C. Keep it alive.** By **March of each odd-numbered year**, present evidence of § 65.91(c)(1)–(4) plus **one** § 65.93(a) activity in year one and **one** in year two.

---

## 6. Common failure points

- Assuming the IA is a rating on the mechanic certificate — it is a separate, expiring **authorization**.
- Treating the § 65.93(a) list as cumulative instead of disjunctive.
- Converting the **per-90-day** rates in § 65.93(a)(1)–(2) into a fixed total for the 2-year period.
- Signing a Form 337 for an alteration performed on **unapproved data** — the most common enforcement exposure.
- Missing the **Part 121 CAMP** carve-out and approving work outside the privilege.
- Letting the mechanic certificate lapse — the IA privileges cannot be exercised unless both ratings are currently effective, regardless of the IA's own date.

---

## 7. Verification notes (read before relying on this)

- **Confirmed verbatim in this packet:** § 65.95(a)(1)–(2); § 65.93(a)(2) (the 'two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days' text); § 65.93 structure as a 2-year renewal with a March-of-odd-year window.
- **Recalled from the regulation and requiring re-verification against the current eCFR page before publication:** the exact paragraph lettering and wording of § 65.91(a), (b), (d); § 65.92 in full; § 65.93(a)(1), (3), (4), (5) and § 65.93(b); § 65.95(b); the Part 43 section-by-section attributions in § 3.
- **Currency:** cite the eCFR text retrieved **2026-11-15** (the § 65.93 page carried a last-updated date of 2026-10-22). IA renewal requirements have changed historically; no historical vintage should be quoted as operative without a separate historical citation.
- **Not sourced here and therefore not asserted:** any earlier version of the renewal thresholds; any claim that the IA privilege extends beyond major repairs/alterations, annual inspections, and progressive inspections; whether Part 121 exclusions map identically into older rule text.

## 8. Scope note (Regulatory Specialist function)

This answer is the regulatory layer only: rule identification, eligibility, privileges and limitations, renewal currency, and citations. It does **not** opine on the airworthiness substantiation of alteration data (stress analysis, flutter, DER/ODA approval, electrical load analysis) — that is engineering-approval work, outside this role. Also outside this answer: repair station approval under Part 145, military/foreign-credential recognition, and any state-level licensing. For the AMT study framing specifically: the FAA AMT handbooks (FAA-H-8083-30/-31/-32) and the IA test supplement are study aids; the legally operative qualifications are the rule text cited above, and the AMT handbooks are not a source of authority.

# Inspection Authorization (IA) and Major Alterations - Qualification Requirements

**Regulatory frame:** Title 14 CFR (eCFR), Parts 1, 43, 65, 91. **'FAA-AMT'** is read as the Aviation Maintenance Technician context (FAA AMT Handbook series, FAA-H-8083-30/-31/-32). The AMT Handbook is explanatory material and is not the rule; the binding requirements are the CFR sections below. FAA handbooks, the IA Information Guide, and advisory circulars are cited only where they interpret a rule.

## 0. Answer in brief

An IA's authority over major alterations rests on four stacked layers of qualification, all in 14 CFR Part 65 Subpart D unless noted:

1. **Certificate layer** - currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** airframe and powerplant ratings, each in effect for a total of at least **3 years** (65.91(c)(1)), kept current under 65.83, and the authorization itself effective under 65.92.
2. **Experience / base / data layer** - at least **2 years** actively engaged in maintaining aircraft (65.91(c)(2)); a fixed base of operations (65.91(c)(3)); and equipment, facilities and **inspection data** available (65.91(c)(4)).
3. **Testing layer** - pass a written test on ability to inspect to safety standards **for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations** and for annual and progressive inspections under Part 43 (65.91(c)(5)). This is the qualification that speaks directly to major alterations.
4. **Exercise layer** - the IA may approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration **only if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**, and may not do so for aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program (65.95; 43.5; 43.7(b); 43.9). Renewal (65.93) requires continuing activity, one accepted route being at least **two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days** the authorization has been held.

A practical summary: the IA is **not** the approver of the alteration design. The design/data must already be FAA-approved (field approval, STC, TC amendment, DER/ODA, PMA, etc.); the IA's qualification is to determine **conformity to that approved data** and to make the airworthiness/return-to-service determination.

## 1. Definition gate - what counts as a 'major alteration'

- **14 CFR 1.1** - *Major alteration* means an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications: (1) that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or (2) that is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations.
- **14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A** - the enumerated lists that make the classification operational: (a) major alterations by product category (airframe, powerplant, propeller, appliance); (b) major repairs; (c) minor repairs/alterations. Appendix A is what an inspector actually works from when the 1.1 test alone is inconclusive.
- **14 CFR 1.1 - 'Approved'** - unless used with reference to another person, means approved by the FAA or by a person to whom the FAA has delegated authority in the matter concerned. This is the hinge for the approved-data requirement in 65.95.

## 2. Layer 1 and 2 - eligibility to hold the authorization (14 CFR 65.91)

| Cite | Requirement |
|---|---|
| 65.91(a) | Application made on the form and in the manner prescribed by the Administrator. |
| 65.91(b) | An applicant who meets the section's requirements is entitled to an inspection authorization. |
| 65.91(c)(1) | Holds a currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and each in effect for a total of at least **3 years**. |
| 65.91(c)(2) | Actively engaged, for at least the **2-year** period before application, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under the chapter. |
| 65.91(c)(3) | Has a fixed base of operations at which the holder may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week (need not be where the authorization is exercised). |
| 65.91(c)(4) | Has available the **equipment, facilities, and inspection data** necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or related parts or appliances. |
| 65.91(c)(5) | **Passes a written test** on ability to inspect according to safety standards **for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations** and for annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43. |
| 65.91(d) | Failure of the (c)(5) test bars reapplication for a stated period (commonly stated as 90 days; a second failure bars reapplication for 1 year) - confirm exact periods in current text. |

Note on 65.91(c)(4): this is the qualification most often failed in practice for major-alteration work. The IA must actually hold the approved technical data for the alteration being inspected. 'I can get it from the installer' is not compliance.

## 3. Duration and currency (65.92, 65.83)

- **65.92 - Duration.** Each inspection authorization expires on **March 31 of each odd-numbered year**; the holder may exercise its privileges only while holding a currently effective mechanic certificate with both a currently effective airframe rating and a currently effective powerplant rating.
- **65.83 - Recent experience.** A mechanic may not exercise certificate privileges unless, within the preceding **24 months**, the Administrator has found the holder able to do the work, or the holder has for at least **6 months** served as a mechanic under the certificate and rating, technically supervised other mechanics, supervised maintenance/alteration in an executive capacity, or a combination. Because 65.92 conditions IA privileges on a currently effective mechanic certificate, 65.83 lapse silently suspends IA authority.

## 4. Layer 3 - renewal (14 CFR 65.93)

Renewal is on a **2-year** cycle keyed to the March 31 odd-year expiration. The applicant must continue to meet the eligibility base (65.91(c)(1)-(4)) and must show recent activity within the 2-year period before application, satisfied by any one of the following routes (verify subparagraph lettering in current text):

1. At least one annual inspection for each **90 days** the authorization has been held; or
2. **At least two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days** the authorization has been held; or
3. Performed or supervised and approved at least one progressive inspection to Administrator-prescribed standards; or
4. Attended and successfully completed a refresher course acceptable to the Administrator of not less than **8 hours** of instruction; or
5. Passed an oral test by an FAA inspector establishing that knowledge of applicable regulations and standards is current.

Route 2 is the direct major-alteration currency path: an IA who does not perform annuals must document major repair/alteration activity at the stated rate to renew.

## 5. Layer 4 - privileges and limitations on major alterations (14 CFR 65.95)

**Privileges (65.95(a)):** the holder may
- inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance after a **major repair or major alteration** accomplished in accordance with Part 43, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator** - subject to the continuous airworthiness maintenance program exception described below; and
- perform an annual inspection, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection, per 43.11, 43.13 and 91.409.

**Limitations (65.95(b) and related):** the holder may **not**
- approve for return to service a major repair or major alteration that was accomplished **without technical data approved by the Administrator**;
- approve major repairs or major alterations on aircraft maintained under a **continuous airworthiness maintenance program** - the regulatory text excepts Part 121 aircraft; FAA guidance and long-standing interpretation state the prohibition for aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness program under Part 121 or 127 (Part 127 has since been removed from the CFR), and the conservative practice is to treat any CAMP aircraft (including Part 135 CAMP) as outside IA approval authority unless the current 65.95(a)(1) text and current IA Information Guide are confirmed to the contrary;
- delegate the inspection. FAA guidance (IA Information Guide) states that a primary IA responsibility is to determine airworthiness by inspecting repairs or alterations for conformity to approved data and assuring the aircraft is in a condition for safe operation; that during inspection of major repairs or major alterations the IA must also determine that they are **compatible with previous repairs and alterations** made to the aircraft; and that the IA must **personally perform** the inspection - the regulations provide no delegation of this responsibility.

## 6. Approvals the IA does not hold

- **Design/data approval.** The IA does not approve alteration data. Alteration data is approved by the FAA (field approval), a DER/ODA, an STC/TC amendment, a PMA/TSO article, or as otherwise permitted (see AC 43-210A for standardized field-approval data request procedures; AC 120-77 for maintenance and alteration data).
- **Who may approve for return to service** after a major repair or alteration is set by **43.7**: the Administrator; the holder of a mechanic certificate or an inspection authorization as provided in Part 65 (43.7(b)); a certificated repair station under Part 145; the manufacturer under 43.3; and other enumerated holders. A mechanic **without** an IA cannot approve a major repair or major alteration for return to service.

## 7. Performance, records and return to service

- **43.13(a)/(b)** - work performed using methods, techniques and practices in the current manufacturer's maintenance manual or Instructions for Continued Airworthiness, or other methods acceptable to the Administrator; and in a manner and with materials such that the condition of the article is **at least equal to its original or properly altered condition** with regard to aerodynamic function, structural strength, resistance to vibration and deterioration, and other qualities affecting airworthiness.
- **43.5** - no person may approve for return to service an aircraft, airframe, engine, propeller, appliance or component part that has undergone maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding or alteration unless the required maintenance record entry has been made, the repair/alteration form furnished or authorized by the Administrator has been executed, and - where the repair or alteration changes operating limitations or approved flight manual data - those limitations/data have been revised and set forth as prescribed in 91.9.
- **43.9** - maintenance record entries; the section carrying the **FAA Form 337 (Major Repair and Alteration)** execution requirement for major repairs and major alterations (confirm the paragraph designator in current text).
- **43.11 / 91.409** - annual and progressive inspection approval standards, which define the parallel IA privilege.

## 8. Point-of-approval procedure for an IA handling a major alteration

1. **Classify.** Apply 14 CFR 1.1 and Part 43 Appendix A. If it is not major, the IA route is not required; if major, every step below applies.
2. **Confirm data approval.** Identify the approved technical data (STC, TC amendment, field approval, DER/ODA approval, etc.). If the alteration was accomplished on acceptable data only, the IA has no authority to approve for return to service (65.95(b)).
3. **Confirm aircraft regime.** If the aircraft is maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program (Part 121; treat Part 135 CAMP conservatively), stop - IA approval authority does not apply.
4. **Inspect conformity personally.** Verify workmanship and conformity to the approved data, including 43.13(b) equal-or-better condition. No delegation.
5. **Check compatibility.** Determine compatibility with all previously accomplished repairs and alterations.
6. **Check collateral effects.** Weight and balance, structural strength, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, operating limitations and flight manual data; revise per 43.5(a)(3) and 91.9 where changed.
7. **Record.** Make the 43.9 entry; ensure Form 337 is executed; make the 43.5 return-to-service approval.
8. **Retain/document.** Keep the approved data, the conformity record and the approval on file for the holder's own 65.91(c)(4)/65.93 evidence trail.

## 9. Frequent disqualifiers and audit findings

- Airframe or powerplant rating lapsed, or the mechanic certificate is not currently effective (65.91(c)(1), 65.92).
- 65.83 recent-experience lapse, which voids exercise of the underlying certificate and therefore the IA privilege.
- Approval for return to service granted on data that is acceptable but not **approved** (65.95(b)).
- Approval granted on a Part 121/CAMP aircraft.
- Approval signed without personal inspection, or 'supervised' to a subordinate.
- Renewal activity not documented in a form that satisfies 65.93.
- Confusing the AMT Handbook's descriptive definition of a major alteration with the controlling 1.1/Appendix A classification.

## 10. Guidance vs. regulation

Binding: 14 CFR 1.1; 43.5; 43.7; 43.9; 43.11; 43.13; Part 43 Appendix A; 65.83; 65.91; 65.92; 65.93; 65.95; 91.9; 91.409. Interpretive/guidance only: FAA IA Information Guide; AMT Handbook (FAA-H-8083-30/-31/-32); AC 43-210A; AC 120-77; AC 43.9-1; FAA Order 8900.1. Guidance may be cited to explain a rule but cannot substitute for it.

## 11. Currency and verification list

This answer is written against the standing text of Part 65 Subpart D and Part 43. Before relying on it in a enforcement-sensitive or certification document, confirm the following against the current eCFR point-in-time text at ecfr.gov: (a) 65.91(d) retest bar periods; (b) the exact 65.93(b)(2) activity sub-items and rates; (c) whether 65.95(a)(1) excepts only Part 121 or also Part 135 CAMPs; (d) the paragraph of 43.9 that carries the Form 337 requirement; (e) the current Appendix A to Part 43 lists. Record the eCFR 'current as of' date in the file when you do.

# Inspection Authorization (IA) and Major Alterations — Qualification Requirements Under 14 CFR (eCFR)

## 0. Scope and reading of the request

- **Source of law:** U.S. Federal Aviation Regulations, 14 CFR, as published on eCFR (https://www.ecfr.gov). No state, foreign, or military rules are covered.
- **"Inspection auth"** = the Inspection Authorization issued under **14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D** (§§ 65.91–65.95).
- **"Major alterations"** = the regulatory meaning in **14 CFR 1.1** (definition) and the enumerated list in **Part 43, Appendix A, paragraph (a)**.
- **"FAA-AMT"** is read as the FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician context (the FAA-H-8083-30/-31/-32 AMT Handbook series and the FAA *Inspection Authorization Information Guide*), i.e., the study/guidance layer that sits on top of the regulation — not a separate regulatory program.
- **Two questions are answered together, because the regulation splits them:**
  1. *Who is qualified to hold an IA at all* → § 65.91 (and § 65.92/§ 65.93 for duration/renewal).
  2. *What that IA is qualified to do specifically with a major alteration* → § 65.95(a)(1), with Part 43 as the performance/return-to-service layer.

## 1. Short answer

A person may inspect and approve a **major alteration** for return to service only if that person holds an **Inspection Authorization** under Part 65 Subpart D. The IA's authority for that act is **14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)**, and it is conditional: the work must have been done **in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**, and the privilege **does not extend to aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness program under Part 121**. A mechanic certificate alone (§ 43.3) does **not** authorize the inspection performed after a major repair or alteration.

To *hold* the IA in the first place, the applicant must satisfy **14 CFR 65.91(a)(1)–(5)** — the five qualification elements, one of which, **(a)(5), is expressly a written test on the ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations**. That paragraph is the direct textual link between "IA qualification" and "major alterations."

## 2. What counts as a major alteration

| Authority | Function |
|---|---|
| **14 CFR 1.1** (definition of *major alteration*) | An alteration not listed in the aircraft/engine/propeller specifications that (1) might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness, or (2) is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations. |
| **14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A, para. (a)** | Enumerated major alterations by airframe, powerplant, propeller, and appliance. Appendix A also carries major repairs (para. (b)) and preventive maintenance (para. (c)). |
| **14 CFR 43.3(a)** | Establishes that the items whose performance constitutes a major alteration/major repair/preventive maintenance are those listed in Appendix A. |

Classification matters because it determines **who may approve for return to service** (§ 43.7 + § 65.95) and **what record must be executed** (§ 43.5(b), FAA Form 337).

## 3. The qualification chain — one table

| # | Question | Governing section | Operative rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Who may *perform* a major alteration? | 14 CFR 43.3 (mechanic/repair station/air agency/manufacturer/repaired per Part 65, 145, etc.) | A certificated mechanic with appropriate ratings may perform alterations under Part 65. **Proviso (quoted from eCFR § 43.3):** "However, this paragraph does not authorize the performance of any inspection required by Part 91 or Part 125 of this chapter or any inspection performed after a major repair or alteration." |
| 2 | Who may *approve for return to service* after a major alteration? | 14 CFR 43.7 (persons authorized to approve for return to service) read with 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1) | The IA holder is the individual who approves major alterations for return to service; a Part 145 repair station may approve work it performed within its ratings. A mechanic acting only under § 43.3 may not. |
| 3 | What are the IA holder's privileges/limits? | 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1) | "Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 of this chapter, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**." |
| 4 | What must the applicant have to *get* the IA? | 14 CFR 65.91(a)(1)–(5) | See § 4 below. |
| 5 | How must the work itself be done? | 14 CFR 43.13(a)–(b) | Use methods/techniques/practices in the current manufacturer's maintenance manual or other methods acceptable to the Administrator; the condition of the article must be at least equal to its original or properly altered condition. |
| 6 | What must be executed/recorded? | 14 CFR 43.5(b); 43.9; 43.11; FAA Form 337 | The repair/alteration form furnished or authorized by the Administrator (Form 337) must be executed in the manner prescribed, and a maintenance record entry made before approval for return to service. |

## 4. IA eligibility qualifications — 14 CFR 65.91(a)

An applicant for an inspection authorization must satisfy **all** of the following (paraphrased; confirm exact wording against the current eCFR text at the URL in § 11):

| Element | Requirement | Why it matters for major alterations |
|---|---|---|
| **65.91(a)(1)** | Hold a **currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating**, each currently effective and in effect for a total of at least **3 years**. | The IA is layered on top of the A&P; there is no stand-alone IA. |
| **65.91(a)(2)** | Have been **actively engaged, for at least the 3-year period before application**, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR. | Practical experience base for judging conformity of altered configurations. |
| **65.91(a)(3)** | Have a **fixed base of operations** at which the holder may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week (it need not be where the authority is exercised). | Traceability/availability of the approving individual. |
| **65.91(a)(4)** | Have available the **equipment, facilities, and inspection data** necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or related parts/appliances. | Major alterations turn on *approved data*; the IA must be able to obtain and use it. |
| **65.91(a)(5)** | **Pass a written test** on the ability to inspect according to **safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations** and annual and progressive inspections under Part 43. | This is the explicit qualification element aimed at major alterations — the knowledge-testable core of the IA credential. |

Duration and renewal (**§ 65.92** and **§ 65.93**) are currency requirements, not major-alteration qualifications; verify their current text on eCFR before relying on any specific period or renewal-activity count, because these have been amended in recent rulemaking cycles.

## 5. The IA privilege for major alterations — 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)

Verified eCFR text (14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)):

> "Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and"

Three qualifications are embedded in that sentence and each must be satisfied before signing:

1. **Credential** — the signer holds a current IA (Part 65 Subpart D).
2. **Approved data** — the alteration was accomplished under **technical data approved by the Administrator** (not merely "acceptable" data; see AC 43-210A for the approved-data hierarchy and field-approval route).
3. **Eligible aircraft** — the aircraft is **not** maintained under a **Part 121 continuous airworthiness program**.

FAA guidance restates the inspection standard the IA is applying:

> "Inspect the configuration of the repair or alteration for conformity to the approved data and the performance standards of 14 CFR part 43." — FAA *Inspection Authorization Information Guide*

## 6. What a mechanic *without* an IA may and may not do

- **May:** perform the alteration work under § 43.3 as a certificated mechanic with the appropriate ratings, under Part 65.
- **May not:** perform the inspection after a major repair or alteration and approve it for return to service. § 43.3 says so expressly: "However, this paragraph does not authorize the performance of any inspection required by Part 91 or Part 125 of this chapter or any inspection performed after a major repair or alteration."
- **Practical consequence:** for a major alteration, the return-to-service signature comes from an IA under § 65.95(a)(1), or from a Part 145 repair station acting within its ratings (§ 43.7 / Part 145), or from another person expressly authorized under § 43.7.

## 7. The data and workmanship standards the IA is certifying to

| Section | Standard |
|---|---|
| **43.13(a)** | Use the methods, techniques, and practices in the current manufacturer's maintenance manual or Instructions for Continued Airworthiness, or other methods acceptable to the Administrator. |
| **43.13(b)** | Work must be done so the condition of the aircraft/article is at least equal to its original or properly altered condition with regard to aerodynamic function, structural strength, resistance to vibration/deterioration, and other airworthiness qualities. |
| **43.5** | No approval for return to service until the maintenance record entry is made and the Administrator's repair/alteration form (FAA Form 337) is executed as prescribed. |
| **43.9** | Content/form/disposition of maintenance and alteration record entries (description, date, signer, certificate number, approval for return to service). |
| **Part 43 App. B** | Recording of major repairs and major alterations (Form 337 disposition). |
| **AC 43.9-1** | Instructions for completing FAA Form 337. |
| **AC 43-210A** | Standardized procedures for requesting approval of data for major repairs/major alterations (approved vs. acceptable data; field approval). |

## 8. Procedure — IA approving a major alteration (operational checklist)

1. **Classify** the work: major vs. minor using 14 CFR 1.1 and Part 43 Appendix A(a). If minor, this procedure does not apply.
2. **Confirm credential currency:** IA issued under Part 65 Subpart D and current per §§ 65.92–65.93; fixed base of operations current per § 65.91(a)(3).
3. **Confirm eligibility of the aircraft:** not maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program (§ 65.95(a)(1) parenthetical).
4. **Obtain and review the approved technical data** for the alteration (STC, TC change, FAA-approved design data, or field-approved data per AC 43-210A). If the data is only "acceptable," the alteration cannot be approved under § 65.95(a)(1) until approval is obtained.
5. **Physically inspect the installation** for conformity to that approved data (configuration, materials, workmanship, clearances, torques, safetying) and against the Part 43 performance standards (§ 43.13).
6. **Verify weight and balance / flight manual implications** and any operating-limitation changes; § 43.5 requires the aircraft to be weighed and the flight manual revised where the alteration changes weight/balance or flight characteristics.
7. **Verify record entries** — maintenance record entry per § 43.9 and FAA Form 337 executed per § 43.5(b) and AC 43.9-1.
8. **Approve for return to service** by signing under § 65.95(a)(1), citing the approved data used.
9. **Retain/distribute records** per § 43.9 and Part 43 Appendix B (Form 337 disposition to the aircraft owner and the FAA).

## 9. Non-IA paths for major alterations (for completeness)

- **Part 145 repair station** — may approve for return to service work it performed, within its ratings and operations specifications (§ 43.7 / Part 145).
- **Manufacturer/TC holder** — via approved design data and production/airworthiness approvals.
- **Field approval** — where no approved data exists, approval of data is obtained from the FAA (AC 43-210A; FAA Order 8900.1 procedures); the IA then inspects against that now-approved data.

## 10. AMT/IA study-guide traps (the "FAA-AMT" layer)

- The IA does **not** get authority from the mechanic certificate; § 43.3 expressly withholds the post-major-repair/alteration inspection.
- The IA privilege is **data-conditional** — "done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator" — not merely "done well."
- The **Part 121 carve-out** is easy to miss.
- A **major alteration is not the same as a major repair**; both fall under § 65.95(a)(1), but they are separately listed in Part 43 Appendix A.
- **Form 337 is a § 43.5 requirement**, not a § 65.95 requirement; the IA's signature and the 337 are two distinct acts.

## 11. Verification checklist (confirm against eCFR before publishing)

| Section | eCFR path | What to confirm |

| 65.91 | https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91 | Exact wording of (a)(1)–(5), including the 3-year thresholds and the (a)(5) test scope. |
| 65.92 / 65.93 | .../section-65.92, .../section-65.93 | Current duration and renewal requirements (recently amended; do not rely on memory). |
| 65.95 | https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.95 | (a)(1) text and Part 121 parenthetical (verified verbatim above). |
| 43.3 | http://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-43/section-43.3 | The proviso quoted above and its **paragraph designator** (cited here as § 43.3 generally, per the eCFR fetch; confirm whether it sits in (b) or another paragraph in the current text). |

| Part 43 App. A / App. B | .../part-43/appendix-A-to-part-43 | Major alteration list and recordkeeping. |
| 14 CFR 1.1 | .../part-1/section-1.1 | Definition of *major alteration*. |
| IA Information Guide | https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/ia_info_guide.pdf | Inspection standard for conformity to approved data and Part 43 performance standards. |

## 12. Caveats

- Text quoted verbatim above is limited to § 65.95(a)(1), the § 43.3 proviso, and the IA Information Guide sentence — all verified from eCFR/FAA fetches. Other sections are described by substance and flagged for paragraph-level confirmation in § 11.
- FAA guidance documents (IA Information Guide, AC 43-210A, AC 43.9-1, FAA Order 8900.1) are **advisory/acceptable means of compliance**; they do not themselves create the qualification. The qualification is created by §§ 65.91 and 65.95.
- Nothing here addresses foreign airworthiness authorities, military airworthiness, or special airworthiness certificate operating limitations that may impose additional alteration-approval constraints.
