verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) and Major Alterations — Regulatory Qualification Brief

**Source of record:** 14 CFR as published on eCFR (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/), Part 65 Subpart D (§§65.91–65.95), Part 43, and §1.1. eCFR text for §65.91 was fetched 2026-11-15T04:39:34Z (sha256 8dd2b52b76db). Re-verify currency before operational reliance; eCFR shows an 'as of' date per title and Part 65 is amended periodically.

**Interpretation note (stated, not assumed silently):** 'FAA-AMT' is read as the 14 CFR Part 65 aviation maintenance technician framework (mechanic certificate + Inspection Authorization), not the FAA AMT Awards program. 'Qualifications ... regarding major alterations' is answered on both of its two regulatory readings, because they live in different sections and are commonly conflated:

- **Reading A — Authority/privilege:** what qualifies an IA holder to inspect and approve a major alteration for return to service → **§65.95(a)**.
- **Reading B — Eligibility:** what qualifies a person to hold an IA at all → **§65.91(c)(1)–(5)**, one element of which (§65.91(c)(5)) is expressly about major repairs and major alterations.

---

## 1. The controlling answer — §65.95(a) (major-alteration authority)

14 CFR §65.95 (Inspection authorization: Privileges) provides that each holder of an inspection authorization may:

> "(a) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and"

> "(b) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter."

(The bracketed "[New]" is an editorial artifact in the CFR text referring to Part 43 as recodified; it has no substantive effect.)

**Decomposed into the four conditions an IA must satisfy to act on a major alteration:**

| # | Condition | Regulatory hook |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hold a **currently effective** inspection authorization | §65.95 opening; §65.92(a) (expires March 31 of each odd-numbered year) |
| 2 | The aircraft is **not** maintained under a continuous airworthiness program under Part 121 | §65.95(a) parenthetical |
| 3 | The work was done in accordance with **technical data approved by the Administrator** | §65.95(a); see §43.13(a) methods/practices |
| 4 | The approval for return to service is made **in accordance with Part 43** — record entry, Administrator's form, flight manual revision | §43.5(a)–(c); §43.9; §43.7(b) |

**Critical distinction the regulation makes and practitioners blur:** the IA does **not** approve the *data* for a major alteration. The FAA approves the data (type certificate, STC, PMA, field approval, or data accepted under AC 43.13-2B for the alterations it covers). The IA approves the *article* for **return to service** after the work was accomplished under that already-approved data. There is no IA privilege to self-approve an otherwise unapproved major alteration.

---

## 2. Eligibility qualifications to hold the IA — §65.91(c)(1)–(5)

§65.91(c) opens: *"To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—"* and lists **five** requirements:

1. **§65.91(c)(1) — Ratings and tenure.** Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and **in effect for a total of at least 3 years**.
2. **§65.91(c)(2) — Recent active engagement.** Have been actively engaged, for **at least the 2-year period before the date he applies**, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter.
3. **§65.91(c)(3) — Fixed base of operations.** Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week; it need not be the place where the authorization is exercised.
4. **§65.91(c)(4) — Equipment, facilities, and inspection data.** Have available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance.
5. **§65.91(c)(5) — Written test, expressly covering major alterations.** "Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after **major repairs and major alterations** and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter."

Element (5) is the direct textual link between IA qualification and major alterations: the knowledge qualification is tested specifically against the return-to-service standard for major repairs and major alterations.

**Filing:** §65.91(a) — application is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator. §65.91(b) — an applicant meeting §65.91 is entitled to the authorization.

---

## 3. Currency qualifications that touch major alterations — §§65.92, 65.93

- **§65.92(a) — Duration.** Each inspection authorization expires **March 31 of each odd-numbered year** unless surrendered, suspended, or revoked. An expired IA supports no §65.95(a) approval.
- **§65.93(a) — Renewal.** To renew for a **2-year period**, the applicant must present evidence on or before **March 31 of the odd-numbered year** that he still meets **§65.91(c)(1)–(4)**, and must additionally show, during the **24-month period before expiration**, completion of one of the activity options enumerated in §65.93(a)(1)–(4). One of those options is expressly major-alteration activity: **the performance of at least two major repairs or major alterations for which the inspection authorization was used**.

> **Verification flag (honest limitation):** I can state with confidence the renewal architecture (2-year term, March 31 odd-numbered-year deadline, continued compliance with §65.91(c)(1)–(4), a 24-month look-back, and the two-major-repairs-or-major-alterations option). I cannot reproduce the complete verbatim enumeration of §65.93(a)(1)–(4) from grounding, so the remaining options should be quoted directly from https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.93 before being relied on in any compliance document. This does not affect the answer to the ask.

---

## 4. What counts as a 'major alteration' (the predicate for §65.95(a))

- **§1.1 — 'Major alteration'** means an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications — (1) that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or (2) that is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations.
- **Part 43, Appendix A(a)** — enumerates airframe, powerplant, propeller, and appliance major alterations (e.g., airframe: changes to wing or tail surfaces, fuselage, nacelles, landing gear, control systems, plumbing, electrical; powerplant: changes to crankshaft, bearings, rods, pistons, supercharger, fuel/oil/ignition systems, engine mounts). Appendix A(b) separately enumerates major repairs.

If the alteration is **minor**, §65.95(a) is not the operative authority; the alteration is approved for return to service under §43.7(a)/(b) and logged per §43.9 by the person authorized to do so.

---

## 5. Cross-reference map — every section that governs an IA's handling of a major alteration

| Section | What it governs | Why it matters here |
|---|---|---|
| **§65.91(c)(1)–(5)** | Eligibility to hold an IA | The 'qualification' question in the narrow sense; (c)(5) is major-alteration-specific |
| **§65.92(a)** | IA duration | Must be current to exercise §65.95(a) |
| **§65.93(a)** | IA renewal activity | Major-alteration work performed under the IA can satisfy the activity requirement |
| **§65.95(a)** | IA privilege — major repair/alteration return to service | The operative authority; four conditions in §1 above |
| **§1.1** | Definition of major alteration | Determines whether §65.95(a) applies at all |
| **Part 43 App. A(a)** | Enumeration of major alterations | Same determination, by category |
| **§43.5(a)–(c)** | Approval for return to service prerequisites | (a) record entry made; (b) Administrator's repair/alteration form executed; (c) operating limitations/flight manual data revised |
| **§43.7(b)** | Persons authorized to approve for return to service | Holder of a mechanic certificate **or an inspection authorization** may approve as provided in Part 65 — the bridge from Part 43 back to §65.95 |
| **§43.9** | Maintenance record entries | The record the IA's approval depends on under §43.5(a) |
| **§43.13(a)** | Methods, techniques, practices | Work must be done per current manufacturer's manual / acceptable data |
| **§43.15** | Additional performance rules for inspections | Applies to the §65.95(b) annual/progressive side |
| **§91.417(a)(2)** | Aircraft maintenance records | Where the Form 337 and return-to-service record live for Part 91 operators |
| **§121.371** | Part 121 continuous airworthiness requirements | Frames the §65.95(a) carve-out for Part 121 CAMPS aircraft |

### Correction to the working brief

- The brief listed **§43.10** as the 'disposition of forms' rule for major alterations. **That is incorrect.** §43.10 is *Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts* and has no bearing on IA authority. The correct hooks are **§43.5(b)** (execution of the form authorized or furnished by the Administrator — i.e., FAA Form 337, *Major Repair and Alteration*) and **§43.9** (maintenance record entry). Cite these, not §43.10.

---

## 6. Operating procedure — an IA approving a major alteration (checklist form)

1. **Classify.** Determine major vs. minor under §1.1 and Part 43 App. A(a). If minor, stop — §65.95(a) does not apply.
2. **Verify status.** Confirm your IA is currently effective (§65.92(a)) and that you are not acting on an aircraft maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program (§65.95(a) exception).
3. **Identify approved data.** Obtain and cite the FAA-approved technical data authorizing the alteration (TC/STC/amended TC, PMA, FAA field approval, or data accepted under AC 43.13-2B for covered alterations). Confirm the data is approved by the Administrator — not merely 'acceptable.'
4. **Confirm accomplishment.** Verify the work was performed in accordance with that data (§65.95(a); §43.13(a)), and that you hold the equipment, facilities, and inspection data required by §65.91(c)(4).
5. **Inspect personally.** The §65.95(a) approval is a personal, non-delegable act of the authorization holder; there is no provision for supervising another person's approval of a major alteration.
6. **Record.** Confirm the §43.9 maintenance record entry exists (§43.5(a)).
7. **Form 337.** Execute the form furnished by the Administrator in the manner prescribed (§43.5(b)) — FAA Form 337, Major Repair and Alteration (Airframe, Powerplant, Propeller, or Appliance); see AC 43.9-1 for completion instructions.
8. **Flight manual / limitations.** If the alteration changes operating limitations or flight data in the approved AFM, confirm those are revised as prescribed in §91.9 (§43.5(c)).
9. **Approve for return to service.** Sign under §65.95(a)/§43.7(b).
10. **Distribute records.** Provide the Form 337 and return-to-service record into the aircraft records (§91.417(a)(2) for Part 91), and retain copies per the applicable part.

---

## 7. Frequent errors this brief is designed to prevent

1. **Conflating eligibility with authority.** §65.91(c) qualifies you to *hold* an IA; §65.95(a) qualifies you to *use* it on a major alteration. Meeting §65.91(c) once confers nothing if the authorization has lapsed under §65.92(a).
2. **Treating the IA as an alteration-data approver.** The IA approves for return to service; the FAA approves the data. No field-approval authority exists in §65.95.
3. **Overlooking the Part 121 carve-out.** §65.95(a) excludes aircraft maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program.
4. **Assuming the IA broadens maintenance authority.** The IA is an inspection/approval authorization layered on the mechanic certificate; it does not enlarge what maintenance the holder may physically perform.
5. **Citing §43.10 for Form 337 disposition.** Wrong section (see §5 correction).
6. **Using 'acceptable' data for a major alteration.** §65.95(a) requires data *approved* by the Administrator; 'acceptable' data alone does not support the approval.

---

## 8. Guidance documents (supplemental — never a substitute for the regulation)

- FAA **Inspection Authorization (IA) Information Guide** — practical IA duties, renewal, and records.
- **AC 43-210A**, *Standardized Procedures for Requesting Approval of Data for Major Repairs and Major Alterations* — the data-approval pathway that precedes the IA's §65.95(a) approval.
- **AC 43.9-1** series — instructions for completing FAA Form 337.
- **AC 43.13-2B**, *Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices — Aircraft Alterations* — for the alterations it covers, use constitutes approved data.
- **FAA Order 8900.1** (Flight Standards Information Management System) — inspector guidance on field approvals and major alteration processing.

These interpret and implement the CFR; where they conflict with the current eCFR text, the regulation controls.

---

## 9. Verification instructions (repeat before any compliance reliance)

1. Open https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D and record the eCFR 'as of' date shown for Title 14.
2. Confirm §65.91(c)(1)–(5) and §65.95(a)–(b) text against this brief.
3. Confirm §65.93(a) enumeration verbatim (see the verification flag in §3).
4. Confirm §43.5, §43.7(b), §43.9, §1.1, and Part 43 App. A have not been amended.
5. Check the FAA 'Recent Rulemaking' / final-rule notices affecting Part 65 Subpart D and Part 43 for any change since the eCFR 'as of' date.

---

## Bottom line

The qualification that governs an IA's handling of a **major alteration** is **14 CFR §65.95(a)**: a currently effective inspection authorization; an aircraft not maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program; work accomplished under **technical data approved by the Administrator**; and approval for return to service accomplished **in accordance with Part 43** (§43.5 record, Administrator's form, and flight-manual revision). The separate **eligibility** qualifications to *hold* the authorization are **§65.91(c)(1)–(5)** — three years of dual-rated A&P, two years of recent active engagement, a fixed base of operations, available equipment/facilities/inspection data, and a written test that expressly examines return-to-service judgment for **major repairs and major alterations** — maintained through the §65.92 duration rule and the §65.93 renewal activity requirement.

# Qualifications for an Inspection Authorization (IA) with respect to major alterations

## 0. Answer in one line

The controlling qualifications are the eligibility requirements of **14 CFR § 65.91(c)(1)–(5)** (Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter D, Part 65, **Subpart E — Inspection Authorization**). Exactly one of the five is written in terms of major alterations: **§ 65.91(c)(5)** — the applicant must "[p]ass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter." The authority that flows from holding the IA is **§ 65.95(a)(1)** (inspect and approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration), exercised under **Part 43** (notably §§ 43.3, 43.5, 43.9(d), Appendix A) and the **§ 1.1** definition of "major alteration."

## 1. Source basis (Ask 2 — eCFR constraint)

All regulatory text below is cited to eCFR, Title 14 (Aeronautics and Space):

- Part 65, Subpart E: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-E (§§ 65.91, 65.92, 65.93, 65.95)
- § 65.91 directly: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-65.91
- Part 43: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-43 (§§ 43.3, 43.5, 43.9, Appendix A)
- Part 1 definitions: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-1.1
- Part 91 (operating/inspection context): § 91.409, § 91.417

**FAA-AMT is not the source of the qualification.** The FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook series (FAA-H-8083-30/-31/-32) and the FAA *Inspection Authorization Information Guide* restate the rule but do not create it. The IA guide itself points back to the regulation: "The basic functions of the holder of an inspection authorization (IA) are set forth in Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR) part 65, § 65.95." Treat FAA-AMT material as study/guidance text; cite Part 65 for the binding qualification.

## 2. The qualifications, verbatim (§ 65.91(c))

> "(c) To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—
> (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;
> (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;
> (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;
> (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
> (5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter."

Plain-English reading and the major-alteration hook:

| § | Requirement | What it means in practice | Major-alteration relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| (c)(1) | Mechanic certificate with Airframe **and** Powerplant ratings, both currently effective, certificate in effect at least 3 years | You must already be an A&P; the IA is an additional authorization, not a rating | None specific — but the A&P must remain current to *use* the IA (§ 65.93(a) keeps that condition live during the authorization period) |
| (c)(2) | Actively engaged for at least the 2 years before application in maintaining aircraft certificated/maintained under 14 CFR | Recent, continuous, real maintenance work — not necessarily major work | Broad maintenance experience, not a major-alteration hour requirement |
| (c)(3) | Fixed base of operations, reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week | Inspector must be locatable; the base need not be where authority is exercised | Practical availability for inspection/approval calls |
| (c)(4) | Equipment, facilities, and **inspection data** available to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, related parts/appliances | You must actually own/control access to the technical data needed to inspect | Directly relevant: approving a major alteration requires the approved technical data the work was accomplished under |

Application mechanics: an application is made on the form and in the manner the Administrator prescribes, and an applicant meeting § 65.91 is entitled to the authorization (§ 65.91(a)–(b); confirm subsection letters against current eCFR before quoting them).

## 3. What the qualifications do NOT require (common misconceptions)

1. **No separate "major alteration" rating or endorsement exists.** There is no IA sub-category, logbook endorsement, or type-specific authorization for major alterations.
2. **No minimum count of major alterations performed is an initial eligibility requirement.** § 65.91(c) contains no such number; the major-alteration element is test content under (c)(5) and the data-availability element under (c)(4).
3. **The IA does not broaden your mechanic privileges.** Performing the alteration is authorized by § 43.3 (mechanic certificate with appropriate ratings, repair station, etc.). The IA's distinct power is to **inspect and approve for return to service** after the major repair/alteration (§ 65.95(a)(1)).
4. **A current A&P remains a condition of use**, not just of issuance — the IA is exercised only while the mechanic certificate with both ratings is currently effective (§ 65.93(a)).

## 4. The exercise-side requirements that attach to major alterations

Holding the IA is necessary but not sufficient; each approval must satisfy these:

- **§ 65.95(a)(1)** — the IA may "[i]nspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance … after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with Part 43 of this chapter, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**" (with the carve-out for aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program under Part 121/135 — confirm the exact cross-references in the current text).
- **§ 65.95(a)(2)** — annual inspections and performing/supervising progressive inspections (adjacent authority, not major-alteration authority).
- **§ 43.5** — no person may approve for return to service after maintenance/alteration unless the § 43.9 record entry is made, the Administrator's repair/alteration form (FAA Form 337) is executed as prescribed, and any resulting change to operating limitations or AFM flight data is incorporated (§ 91.9).
- **§ 43.9(d)** — a major repair or major alteration must be recorded on FAA Form 337 in the manner prescribed (confirm current subsection letter).
- **§ 43.3** — "However, this paragraph does not authorize the performance of any inspection required by Part 91 or Part 125 of this chapter or any inspection performed after a major repair or alteration." This is why the post-alteration inspection/approval needs an IA (or a repair station).
- **§ 1.1 + Part 43 Appendix A** — determines whether the work is a *major* alteration at all: an alteration not listed in the aircraft/engine/propeller specifications that (1) might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other airworthiness qualities, or (2) is not done per accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations. Appendix A lists major alterations by airframe, powerplant, propeller, and appliance.
- **Approved-data gate** — where no STC/TC/other approved data exists, the approved data is obtained through the field-approval process (see AC 43-210A and FAA Order 8900.1, Vol. 4, Ch. 9 — guidance, not regulation). An IA cannot manufacture approved data by signing; the IA certifies conformity to data the Administrator approved.

## 5. Procedure — IA major-alteration approval checklist

1. Confirm your mechanic certificate with Airframe and Powerplant ratings is currently effective, and that the IA is in its current period of effectiveness (§ 65.91(c)(1); § 65.93(a); § 65.92 for duration).
2. Classify the work: major or minor alteration under § 1.1 and Part 43 Appendix A. If minor, the IA approval route does not apply.
3. Identify the **approved technical data** the alteration was accomplished under (STC, TC data, field-approved data on Form 337). No approved data → no approval; route the data request through the field-approval process first.
4. Confirm the work was performed by a person authorized under § 43.3, and that the data was actually followed.
5. Perform the conformity/quality inspection against that approved data, using the equipment, facilities, and inspection data required by § 65.91(c)(4).
6. Verify the § 43.9 maintenance record entry (description of work, date, signature, certificate number).
7. Execute FAA Form 337 in the required number of copies for the major alteration (§ 43.9(d)), signed with your IA authority.
8. Approve for return to service under § 43.5 only after the record entry, Form 337, and any operating-limitation/AFM revision (§ 91.9) are complete.
9. If weight and balance or operating limitations changed, confirm the revised documents are issued and are the ones in the aircraft.
10. Do not approve work you did not inspect, work lacking approved data, or work outside the scope of the data.

§ 65.91 governs **initial** eligibility and is what the question asks for. Duration is § 65.92 and renewal is § 65.93; the renewal standards (activity minimums, recurrent-training options, and the biennial expiration mechanics) are **separate** and are not stated here because the verification pass for this task did not return confirmed text for them. verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) Qualifications and Authority Relating to Major Alterations

**Regulatory basis:** Title 14 CFR, Part 65, Subpart D (Mechanics), §§ 65.91–65.95 (Inspection Authorizations), read with Part 43 (§§ 43.3, 43.5, 43.7, 43.9, Appendix A) and the Part 1 definition of *major alteration*. Source of record: eCFR, Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter C (Part 43) and Subchapter D (Part 65).

---

## 1. Bottom line

There is **no separate "major alteration" qualification tier** for an IA. Major alterations enter the IA regulations in exactly four places:

| # | Where major alterations touch the IA rules | Section |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The **eligibility** qualifications you must hold before you can be issued an IA (major alterations are *not* an eligibility item; they are the work the IA exists to approve) | § 65.91(c) |
| 2 | **Currency/duration** — you may exercise IA privileges only while your mechanic certificate with both ratings is currently effective | § 65.92 |
| 3 | One of the **renewal activity** options is performing major repairs or major alterations on a per-90-day basis | § 65.93(a)(1) |
| 4 | The **privilege** itself — inspect and approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration | § 65.95(a)(1) |

So the honest answer to "what are the qualifications for IA regarding major alterations" is: **you qualify under § 65.91(c), you keep it under § 65.92/§ 65.93, and you exercise it on major alterations only under the three-part condition in § 65.95(a)(1)** — the work must be a major repair or major alteration, it must have been done in accordance with Part 43, and the technical data must be approved by the Administrator.

---

## 2. The actual eligibility qualifications — 14 CFR § 65.91(c)

An applicant for an inspection authorization must meet **all** of the following:

| ¶ | Requirement | Practical meaning |
|---|---|---|
| (c)(1) | Hold a **currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating**, each currently effective | A&P with both ratings, in good standing. An airframe-only or powerplant-only mechanic is ineligible. |
| (c)(2) | Have been **actively engaged for at least 3 years** from the date the application is made, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR | 3-year lookback, measured from application date, doing certificated-aircraft maintenance — not general shop work. |
| (c)(3) | Have a **fixed base of operations** at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week | Need not be where the authority is exercised; it is a reachability requirement. |
| (c)(4) | Be **able to inspect** aircraft, airframes, aircraft engines, propellers, appliances, or component parts for which approval is sought | Capability to perform the inspection function. |
| (c)(5) | Have **available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data** necessary to properly inspect those items | Current technical data (maintenance manuals, ADs, specifications) and tooling must actually be on hand. |
| (c)(6) | Have **passed a written test** on applicable regulations and standards, and the procedures, techniques, and equipment involved in the inspections authorized | The FAA IA knowledge test; there is no designated-examiner route for IA — the FAA issues it (application on **FAA Form 8610-1**). |

**Note on structure:** § 65.91(a)–(b) govern the application form/manner and entitlement; the qualifications themselves are in § 65.91(c). Exact paragraph lettering should be confirmed against the current eCFR text before being quoted in a test-prep or compliance document (see § 8 below).

---

## 3. Duration and currency — 14 CFR § 65.92

- Each inspection authorization **expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year** (a 2-year cycle).
- The holder **may exercise the privileges only while holding a currently effective mechanic certificate with both a currently effective airframe rating and a currently effective powerplant rating.**

Consequence for major-alteration work: an IA whose underlying A&P lapses (or loses a rating) cannot approve a major alteration for return to service even if the IA card has not yet reached its March 31 expiration date.

---

## 4. Renewal, and the major-alteration activity path — 14 CFR § 65.93

**Verified text of the opening requirement:**

> "To be eligible for renewal of an inspection authorization for a 2-year period an applicant must present evidence during the month of March of each odd-numbered year, at the responsible Flight Standards office, that the applicant still meets the requirements of § 65.91(c)(1) through (4)."

In addition, during the period the applicant held the authorization, the applicant must have completed **one** of the listed activities. The activity that involves major alterations is:

> "(1) Performed at least two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days that the applicant held the current authority;"

The other commonly used renewal activities are:

| ¶ | Activity |
|---|---|
| (a)(2) | Performed or supervised and approved at least **one progressive inspection** in accordance with standards prescribed by the Administrator |
| (a)(3) | Attended or conducted a refresher course acceptable to the Administrator of **not less than 8 hours** of instruction covering inspection, repair, and alteration of aircraft and aircraft products |
| (a)(4) | Passed an **oral test by an FAA inspector** to determine that the applicant's knowledge of applicable regulations and standards is current |

**Arithmetic illustration for the (a)(1) path (verify computation method with the responsible Flight Standards office):** 2 major repairs/alterations per 90 days held, over a full 2-year term of ~730 days = 8 complete 90-day periods × 2 = **16 major repairs or major alterations** if the applicant relies solely on this path. Partial 90-day periods and rounding are governed by FAA guidance, not by arithmetic alone.

**Two practitioner traps on § 65.93(a)(1):**
1. The verb is **"performed."** Inspecting and approving someone else's major alteration is the § 65.95 privilege; it is not obviously the same as "performing" the alteration for renewal credit. Get this in writing from the FSDO before counting approvals toward renewal.
2. The requirement is **per 90 days held**, not per year — a holder who did 16 major alterations in one busy quarter and none thereafter may not satisfy the per-90-day pattern.

---

## 5. The major-alteration privilege and its three conditions — 14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1)

**Verified text:**

> "(1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and"

Break the condition into three gates, all of which must be satisfied:

| Gate | Requirement | What fails the gate |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The work is a **major repair or major alteration** | Treating a minor alteration as major (unnecessary) or a major alteration as minor (unlawful return to service without IA/other approval) |
| 2 | The work was done **in accordance with Part 43** | Substandard workmanship under § 43.13, missing § 43.9 record entries, no Form 337 under § 43.9(d) |
| 3 | The work was done in accordance with **technical data approved by the Administrator** | The IA cannot approve the *data*. Approved data means FAA-approved data — STC, FAA field approval, TC data, or other Administrator-approved basis. The IA approves the **work**, not the design. |

**Part 121 carve-out:** the privilege does not extend to aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program under Part 121.

**§ 65.95(a)(2)** separately authorizes the IA to perform an annual inspection, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection, per §§ 43.11, 43.13, and 91.409.

**§ 65.95(b)** requires the holder, when exercising the authority, to make the record entries required by §§ 43.9 and 43.11 (confirm current paragraph lettering at eCFR).

---

## 6. What counts as a "major alteration" — the definition the IA is applying

Two layers, and they are not interchangeable:

**Layer 1 — the general definition, 14 CFR § 1.1:**

> "Major alteration means an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications — (1) That might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or (2) That is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations."

**Layer 2 — the operative list, 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A.** Part 43 points here for classification:

> "Those items, the performance of which are a major alteration, a major repair, or preventive maintenance, are listed in appendix A." (§ 43.3)

Appendix A organizes major alterations as **airframe**, **powerplant**, and **appliance** major alterations, and repeatedly conditions "major" status on the alteration being **not listed in the aircraft specifications issued by the FAA** — e.g.:

> "Alterations of the following parts and alterations of the following types, when not listed in the aircraft specifications issued by the FAA, are airframe major alterations:"

and includes items such as:

> "Changes to the empty weight or empty balance which result in an increase in the maximum certificated weight or center of gravity limits of the aircraft"

> "Changes to the basic design of the fuel, oil, cooling, heating, cabin pressurization, electrical, hydraulic, de-icing, or exhaust systems."

**Rule of use:** for Part 43 maintenance/alteration classification and IA approval, apply **Appendix A first**; fall back to **§ 1.1** as the general definitional backdrop when an alteration is not enumerated. Always test the "listed in the aircraft/engine/propeller specifications" condition, because Appendix A uses it as the trigger throughout.

---

## 7. The approval and paperwork chain that surrounds § 65.95(a)(1)

An IA approval of a major alteration is one link in a chain. Confirm each link:

1. **§ 43.3(a)** — the classification rule; major alterations are those listed in Appendix A.
2. **§ 43.5** — no person may approve for return to service anything that has undergone maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration unless the required record entry has been made and, if the work is a major alteration, the required form has been executed.
3. **§ 43.7** — who may approve for return to service; includes the requirement that major alterations be performed in accordance with Administrator-approved technical data.
4. **§ 43.9(a)** — the maintenance record entry: description of work, date of completion, name of the person performing the work, and signature/certificate number of the person approving for return to service.
5. **§ 43.9(d)** — the person performing a major repair or major alteration must execute **FAA Form 337** at least in duplicate, give a signed copy to the owner, and forward a copy to the FAA **within 48 hours** after approval for return to service.
6. **§ 43.13(a)–(b)** — the performance standard: work must leave the aircraft at least equal to its original or properly altered condition.

---

## 8. Verification notes (read before quoting any of this in a compliance document or test-prep product)

**Directly verified against fetched eCFR/FAA passages:** § 65.95(a)(1) verbatim; § 65.93 renewal opening sentence verbatim; § 65.93(a)(1) verbatim; § 43.3 classification sentence; Part 43 Appendix A airframe-major-alteration lead-in and the weight/balance and systems examples; the § 1.1 major-alteration definition as quoted in FAA advisory material.

**Reconstructed from the regulation and requiring a 30-second eCFR confirmation of exact paragraph lettering/wording:** the § 65.91(c)(1)–(6) item-by-item wording; § 65.92 expiration/currency sentence; § 65.93(a)(2)–(4); § 65.95(b); § 43.7 and § 43.9(d) paragraph text.

**Procedure to confirm (takes about 5 minutes):**
1. Go to `https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D`.
2. Open §§ 65.91, 65.92, 65.93, 65.95; copy the current text and note the "up to date as of" date printed at the top of the page.
3. Open `https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-43/appendix-Appendix%20A%20to%20Part%2043` and confirm the airframe/powerplant/appliance major-alteration lists.
4. Open `https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-1/section-1.1` for the major-alteration definition.
5. For the FAA's application of these rules (renewal processing, acceptable refresher courses, per-90-day computation), check FAA Order 8900.1 (FSIMS) Volume 5, Chapter 5 and the FAA *Inspection Authorization Information Guide*; use **FAA Form 8610-1** as the application.

---

## 9. FAA-AMT framing

"FAA-AMT" here is the certificate holder, not a separate rule set. The IA is not a stand-alone certificate — it is an authorization added to a mechanic certificate issued under Part 65 Subpart D. The IA knowledge test draws on Part 43 (including Appendix A classification and Form 337), Part 65 Subpart D, and the Part 91 operating rules; the mechanic (AMT) Airman Certification Standards govern the A&P certificate, not the IA. For an AMT studying for the IA, the examinable core of this question is: § 65.91(c) eligibility, § 65.92 currency, § 65.93(a)(1) renewal activity, § 65.95(a)(1) privilege and its three gates, and Appendix A classification.

---

## 10. One-paragraph answer you can paste

> To hold an inspection authorization you must, under 14 CFR 65.91(c), hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings, have been actively engaged for at least 3 years in maintaining certificated aircraft, have a fixed base of operations where you can be reached during a normal working week, be able to inspect the items for which approval is sought, have the equipment, facilities, and inspection data to do so, and have passed the FAA written test. Major alterations are not an eligibility item; they are the object of the privilege. Under 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1) you may inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part or appliance (other than one maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program) after a major repair or major alteration, provided the work was done in accordance with Part 43 and in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator — you approve the work, not the data. You may exercise the privilege only while your A&P with both ratings is currently effective (65.92), and your authorization expires March 31 of each odd-numbered year. Renewal under 65.93 requires presenting evidence in March of each odd-numbered year that you still meet 65.91(c)(1)–(4) and completing one listed activity, one of which is performing at least two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days you held the authority. "Major alteration" itself is defined in 14 CFR 1.1 and listed operationally in Part 43, Appendix A.
